bull.b: FDA approval converts apitegromab from a development program into a commercial product and supports immediate U.S. launch activity. This creates a potential recurring revenue base, strengthens Scholar Rock’s position in neuromuscular disease, and provides a foundation for broader physician and payer adoption.

The pivotal efficacy result provides a durable clinical rationale for using ISEMBYLD alongside SMN2-targeted therapy. Demonstrated motor-function improvement can support physician confidence, payer discussions, and patient uptake while differentiating the product within the SMA treatment landscape.

A sizable cash balance and additional financing levers give Scholar Rock resources to support commercialization, regulatory obligations, and pipeline development. This liquidity should reduce immediate funding pressure and provide flexibility while the company works to establish product revenue and manage launch costs.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and widening losses
bear.b: Scholar Rock remains dependent on external funding because operating and free cash flow are deeply negative while losses continue to widen. Sustained spending on research and commercialization could consume liquidity, increase financing needs, and limit the company’s flexibility if product revenue ramps slowly.

bear.t: Post-marketing safety obligations and fracture monitoring
bear.b: The required pregnancy study and accelerated fracture reporting create ongoing regulatory, operational, and reputational obligations after approval. The safety-monitoring burden may increase costs and could affect physician or payer confidence if additional fracture-related findings emerge during broader real-world use.

bear.t: Payer access may slow early adoption
bear.b: Prior-authorization requirements and expected early reimbursement friction could delay treatment starts even after FDA approval. Longer prescription-to-infusion cycles may slow revenue conversion, increase support costs, and make the commercial ramp less predictable during the product’s first months in the market.
